DEEP PIXEL-PERFECT AUDIT AND FIX. Compare every homepage section against the Webflow source and fix ALL discrepancies. No planning — read, compare, fix.

Project: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Boldteq/`

## Process
For EACH homepage section:
1. Read the Webflow HTML section from `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Boldteq/boldteq-v1-0.webflow/index.html`
2. Grep the exact CSS classes used from `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Boldteq/boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css`
3. Read the current Next.js component
4. Compare every CSS property and fix discrepancies

## Files to audit and fix:
- `src/components/home/hero.tsx` — check against `section-high-judge home-ban-judge` classes
- `src/components/home/typewriter.tsx` — check animation matches Webflow typewriter behavior
- `src/components/home/featured-logos.tsx` — check against logo section classes, image paths
- `src/components/home/portfolio-carousel.tsx` — check against `img-slider-sec` classes, slide sizes, dot styles
- `src/components/home/pain-points.tsx` — check against `slowing-sec` classes, card styles, hover effects
- `src/components/home/resolution-banner.tsx` — check against `blue-card-sec` classes
- `src/components/home/built-for.tsx` — check against `built-seccc` classes
- `src/components/home/benefits-grid.tsx` — check against `works-sec` classes, card grid, image sizes
- `src/components/home/how-it-works.tsx` — check against `blue-sec makeit-sec` classes, step layout
- `src/components/home/pricing-section.tsx` — check against `new-price-sec` classes, tab styles, card layout, comparison table
- `src/components/home/comparison.tsx` — check against `ways-sec` classes, chat bubble styles
- `src/components/home/faq-section.tsx` — check against `faq-section home-faq` classes, accordion styling

## What to verify for EACH section:
- Section padding (Webflow uses `padding: XXpx 5%` pattern)
- Max-width containers
- Heading: exact font-size, font-weight, line-height, color, margin-bottom
- Body text: exact font-size, line-height, color, max-width
- Card styles: exact padding, border-radius, shadow, border, background
- Card hover: exact hover background, border-color, transition duration
- Button styles: exact padding, border-radius, gradient, font-size, font-weight
- Image sizes: exact width, height, object-fit, border-radius
- Grid/flex layouts: exact columns, gaps, alignment
- Spacing between elements: exact margins and gaps
- Background colors: exact hex values
- Responsive breakpoints: check 991px, 767px, 479px media queries

## Also check:
- Are all image paths correct? Do the referenced images exist in `/public/images/webflow/`?
- Is any text different from the Webflow source? Must be word-for-word identical.
- Are any sections missing content that exists in the Webflow HTML?
- Remove any placeholder/emoji icons — use actual images from `/images/webflow/` 
- Remove any hardcoded content that should come from constants

## Rules
- Use Edit for surgical fixes
- Match Webflow CSS EXACTLY
- Clean up unused imports/code
- No `any` types
- Ensure all `"use client"` directives are only where needed
- Check that framer-motion animations don't conflict with the design

FIX EVERYTHING. Don't just report — fix it.

1	---
2	name: Yash Baldha Profile
3	description: Who Yash is, how he works, and what he expects — apply this to all interactions
4	type: user
5	---
6	
7	## Role
8	Founder & CEO of Boldteq. Runs an agency (white-label execution) while building a software factory that mass-produces SaaS products across all industries.
9	
10	## How He Works
11	- Gives 1-2 line briefs and expects full production-grade output
12	- Does not code, design, or do operational tasks — that's the agent team's job
13	- Makes decisions, sets direction, approves plans
14	- Wants speed + quality simultaneously — not one or the other
15	
16	## What He Expects From Agents
17	- Read the brief, research the market, architect the solution, build it, test it, ship it
18	- No repeated explanations — if it's in memory, apply it silently
19	- No asking for obvious next steps — just execute
20	- No templated output, no filler, no generic plans
21	- Everything premium and branded — never looks like a demo or template
22	
23	## Communication Style
24	- Short and direct — every word earns its place
25	- Bullet points over paragraphs
26	- Show the work (code, output) — don't explain the work
27	- Never recap what you just did at the end of a response
28	
29	## Business Context
30	- Building multiple products simultaneously
31	- Goal: dramatically reduce time-to-launch through accumulated agent knowledge
32	- Believes in complexity as a competitive moat
33	- Ships v1 fast (branded + functional + deployable), then iterates to v2/v3
34	- Target: build any production app in 1-2 weeks, improving with every build

3	description: Direct corrections and guidance from Yash — apply these immediately and always. Highest priority memory.
4	type: feedback
5	priority: critical
6	---
7	
8	## How This File Works
9	- Every correction Yash makes gets logged here with context
10	- These override any other pattern or agent behavior
11	- Agents must check this file before executing any task
12	- Quill updates copy patterns, Mira propagates to affected agents

14	---
15	
16	## ★ CRITICAL 2026-04-10 — STACK A MIGRATION (LOVABLE → NEXT.JS + RAILWAY)
17	
18	**Date:** 2026-04-10
19	**Directive:** Boldteq is done with Lovable for internal SaaS products. ALL new SaaS products use **Next.js 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo Payments**.
20	
21	**The exact stack (locked, no deviation):**
22	- Framework: **Next.js 16.2.3** (App Router only, no Pages Router)
23	- Runtime: React 19, TypeScript strict, Node 20 LTS, pnpm 9
24	- Styling: Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui (Vega owns tokens)
25	- Database: **Supabase** (Postgres + Auth + Storage, RLS mandatory)
26	- Hosting: **Railway** — frontend, API routes, workers, cron, Redis — ALL on Railway
27	- Billing: **Dodo Payments** (NEVER Stripe for Boldteq products)
28	- Email: Resend. Errors: Sentry. Analytics: PostHog. Logs: pino.
29	
30	**Topology:**
31	- Frontend → Next.js on Railway
32	- Backend → Next.js API routes on same Railway service
33	- Workers → separate Railway services (BullMQ + Redis, private networking)
34	- Database → Supabase managed (never self-hosted)
35	- Auth → Supabase Auth (`@supabase/ssr`, NEVER deprecated `auth-helpers-nextjs`)
36	- Storage → Supabase Storage with RLS + signed URLs
37	
38	**What's forbidden for Stack A:**
39	- ❌ Vercel (Railway only)
40	- ❌ Stripe (Dodo only)
41	- ❌ Prisma, Drizzle, or any alt ORM (Supabase client only)
42	- ❌ NextAuth (Supabase Auth only)
43	- ❌ Pages Router (`pages/` directory)
44	- ❌ `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` (deprecated)
45	- ❌ npm/yarn (pnpm only)
46	- ❌ CSS modules / styled-components / Emotion
47	- ❌ `any` types / `console.log` in production code / `@ts-ignore`
48	- ❌ Self-hosted Postgres
49	- ❌ AWS Lambda / Cloudflare Workers for app logic
50	
51	**Lovable handling:**
52	- All Lovable stack knowledge **archived** to `stacks/_archive/lovable/`
53	- All Lovable patterns **archived** to `patterns/_archive/lovable/`
54	- Rankora + CROBOT are **grandfathered** (maintained as Lovable, NOT rebuilt)
55	- Rex must NEVER route new Boldteq builds to Lovable
56	- Only load Lovable files if user explicitly mentions "Lovable" or a client requests it
57	
58	**Railway patterns agents must know:**
59	- GitHub push → Railway auto-deploy (main → prod, develop → staging)
60	- Preview environment per PR (Railway preview + Supabase DB branching)
61	- Private networking between services (REDIS_PRIVATE_URL)
62	- Custom domains with auto SSL
63	- Rollback via `railway rollback`
64	- Service separation: web + worker-jobs + worker-cron + redis
65	
66	**Production infra patterns agents must enforce:**
67	- Env vars: multi-env (production/staging/preview), scoped properly
68	- Logging: structured (pino), never `console.log`
69	- Rate limiting: every public API route (Upstash Redis)
70	- Caching: Next `unstable_cache` + Redis + client-side (SWR/TanStack)
71	- Health checks: `/api/health` required (Railway healthcheck path)
72	- Job queues: BullMQ with retry + dead letter queue
73	- RLS: mandatory on every Supabase table, Sage blocks deploy if missing
74	- Monitoring: Sentry (full stack) + PostHog + Railway logs + BetterStack uptime
75	
76	**Source of truth:** `~/.claude/memory/stacks/saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md`
77	
78	**Impact:** ALL 21 agents were retrained on this migration 2026-04-10. Any agent file that still mentions Lovable or Vercel for NEW builds is a bug — report to Mira immediately.

82	## UI/UX Corrections
83	
84	### Never Look AI-Generated
85	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
86	- **Context:** Core brand requirement
87	- **Rule:** Every UI must look custom-built, never like a template or AI output
88	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing), Riko (scaffolding)
89	- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md` for full checklist
90	
91	### Follow Top SaaS Brand Patterns
92	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
93	- **Context:** Quality bar is Linear, Notion, Vercel, Dodo Payments — not generic SaaS
94	- **Rule:** Every design decision should reference what proven SaaS companies do
95	- **Applies to:** All agents that produce user-facing output
96	- **Reference:** See `patterns/good/saas-brand-patterns.md`
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Communication Corrections
101	
102	### Don't Explain — Execute
103	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
104	- **Context:** Yash gives short briefs and expects full execution, not questions
105	- **Rule:** Don't ask for permission on obvious next steps. Don't recap. Don't explain what you're about to do — just do it.
106	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Rex
107	
108	### Show Work, Not Words
109	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
110	- **Context:** Output code, files, deployed URLs — not paragraphs explaining the plan
111	- **Rule:** Minimize narrative. Maximize artifacts.
112	- **Applies to:** All agents
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Architecture Corrections
117	
118	### Every SaaS Must Ship with Admin Panel, Billing, and Complete Pages
119	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
120	- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
121	- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
122	- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
123	- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence
124	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Arya (architecture), Koda (building), Sage (review), Rex (orchestration)
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Process Corrections
129	
130	### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
131	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
132	- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
133	- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
134	- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data
135	- **Rule:** If an agent cannot verify (e.g., no running server), it must explicitly state "unverified" rather than "done"
136	- **Applies to:** All agents
137	
138	---
139	
140	## Project-Specific Rules
141	
142	### Lovable Projects — Don't Break Structure
143	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
144	- **Context:** Yash sometimes builds initial versions in Lovable, then opens in VS Code + Claude Code for editing
145	- **Rule:** NEVER restructure a Lovable project's folders. Keep pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, hooks in `src/hooks/`, utils in `src/lib/`. The `src/integrations/supabase/` folder is sacred — don't touch `client.ts` or `types.ts`.
146	- **Rule:** No Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components. It's Vite + React SPA.
147	- **Rule:** All imports use `@/` alias. Migrations use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql`.
148	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Lovable-origin projects
149	
150	### Shopify Apps — Polaris ONLY, No Exceptions
151	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
152	- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
153	- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
154	- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.
155	- **Rule:** Billing MUST use Shopify Billing API — NEVER use Dodo Payments or any external payment provider for Shopify app charges.
156	- **Rule:** GDPR webhooks (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) must be implemented even if no data is stored.
157	- **Rule:** Every database query must be scoped by `shop` from `session.shop`.
158	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Stack B (Shopify) projects
159	
160	## Navigation & Sidebar Corrections
161	
162	### No Duplicate Navigation Destinations
163	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
164	- **Context:** Admin sidebar footer had a user menu card identical to the topbar dropdown. Settings appeared in both sidebar nav and topbar dropdown. Admin Panel link was in both sidebar footer and topbar dropdown.
165	- **Rule:** Each navigation destination appears in exactly ONE place. If it is in the sidebar, remove it from the topbar dropdown. If it is in the topbar, remove it from the sidebar. No exceptions.
166	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing)
167	
168	### Admin Sidebar Must Match User Sidebar Components
169	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
170	- **Context:** Koda built admin sidebar as a custom `<aside>` element while the user sidebar already used shadcn `Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider`. Yash: "use exactly the same components, css as user sidebar."
171	- **Rule:** When both admin and user sidebars exist in the same app, they MUST use the identical component system. Only nav items and footer content differ. Never build a second sidebar with different components.
172	- **Rule:** Before building any sidebar, CHECK what the existing sidebar in the project uses. Reuse it.
173	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Arya (architecture)
174	
175	### Collapsible Config Pages Use Rows, Not Card Grids
176	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 3 + 7, recurring preference)
177	- **Context:** Koda defaulted to card grids for admin config/integration pages. Yash prefers collapsible rows for these pages.
178	- **Rule:** Admin configuration, integration, and settings pages should use collapsible row layouts, NOT card grids. Card grids are for dashboards and marketing pages.
179	- **Applies to:** Koda (building)
180	
181	---
182	
183	## Version Verification Corrections
184	
185	### ALWAYS Verify Latest Stable Version Before Specifying One
186	- **Date:** 2026-04-10 (Rankora → Next.js migration plan review)
187	- **Context:** I wrote a Rankora migration plan specifying "Next.js 14 App Router" throughout, without checking the npm registry. Yash asked "why we using next js 14? there already latest version available right?" I ran `npm view next version` → **16.2.3** was the actual latest. Next 15 shipped Oct 2024. I was TWO major versions behind, defaulting to a training-data memory instead of checking reality. Yash pushed back twice: "why you choose 14 i dont say than why use 14? give me source and reason." I had no valid reason — it was lazy default, not a decision.
188	- **Rule:** Before recommending or using a specific version of ANY framework, library, or major dependency in a plan or implementation, ALWAYS run `npm view <pkg> version` AND `npm view <pkg> dist-tags` to verify the actual current stable. Cite the output in the plan. Do NOT default to versions from training data.
189	- **Why:** This directly violates the CLAUDE.md rule "Latest stable versions always — no legacy patterns, no deprecated APIs." Plans with wrong versions cascade: wrong breaking changes, wrong peer deps, wrong docs, wasted research, lost credibility.
190	- **How to apply:**
191	  1. Any time a plan or code mentions a version number for Next.js, React, Node, Supabase, Prisma, Shopify CLI/Polaris, Tailwind, Vite, AI SDKs, etc. → run `npm view <pkg> version` FIRST.
192	  2. For peer compatibility, run `npm view <pkg> peerDependencies` on every major dep before locking.
193	  3. Same applies to other ecosystems: `pip index versions <pkg>`, `cargo search <pkg>`, `gem list <pkg> --remote --exact`, `go list -m -versions <mod>`.
194	  4. If you cannot verify (no network, offline), say so **explicitly** instead of guessing: "Could not verify latest — assuming X, verify before install."
195	  5. When stating a version, include the source: "Next.js 16.2.3 (confirmed via `npm view next version` on 2026-04-10)."
196	- **Applies to:** ALL agents — Arya (architecture), Riko (scaffold), Koda (build), Rex (orchestration), Nova (research). Especially critical for any plan that specifies a scaffold command or `package.json` content.
197	
198	---
199	
200	## Training Pass 2 Invariants (2026-04-11)
201	
202	### Never Fabricate Project Names, Training Targets, or Live Demos
203	- **Date:** 2026-04-11
204	- **Context:** During Training Pass 2, a project name was fabricated as a "live training ground" and inserted into memory, agent scenarios, HEALTH.md, and the claude-hub HTML without Yash approving it as a real product. Yash deleted it twice and required a full erase.
205	- **Rule:** Agents may NOT invent project names, fabricate live training targets, or insert imaginary products into any registry, memory file, agent scenario, or HTML dashboard. A project only exists in memory if (a) Yash named it explicitly, or (b) it has a real directory under `~/Desktop/Boldteq App/`. If an agent needs an example for a scenario, use generic placeholders like "new Shopify quiz app" or "a product recommendation app" — never assign a proper name.
206	- **Applies to:** ALL agents — especially Arya, Koda, Rex, Mira (which rebuilds project registries), and any scenario or example block in agent training data.
207	
208	### Agent Class Caps Are Non-Negotiable
209	- **Date:** 2026-04-11 (Training Pass 2)
210	- **Context:** Hardened 8 agents with executable auto-fix loops. Class caps enforced: Builder $5 / 25 min / 5 retries. Gate $3 / 15 min / 3 retries. Planner $3-4 / 15-90 min / 3 retries. Insight $3 / 10 min / 3 retries.
211	- **Rule:** Every agent must load `patterns/good/executable-auto-fix-loop.md` at start of work and enforce its own class cap. If wall-clock or cost cap trips, escalate with the standard escalation JSON — do NOT silently continue or exceed the cap.
212	- **Applies to:** ALL 21 agents.
213	
214	### Git Autonomy Is Feature-Branch Only — Never Main, Never Direct
215	- **Date:** 2026-04-11
216	- **Context:** Training Pass 2 granted full commit+push autonomy to agents. This autonomy is feature-branch scoped.
217	- **Rule:** Agents commit to `agent/<name>/<slug>-<ts>` or `koda/<slug>-<date>` branches only. Never commit to `main` of product repos. Never force-push. Use conventional commits. Open PRs as draft via `gh pr create --draft`. Mira's weekly sweep is the only exception: it may commit directly to `main` of the memory repo (not product repos) with message `mira(sweep): <ISO>`.
218	- **Applies to:** ALL agents with write access.
219	
220	### Stack A Is Locked to Next 16.2.3 + Supabase + Railway + Dodo
221	- **Date:** 2026-04-10 (locked), 2026-04-11 (reaffirmed)
222	- **Context:** Stack A master file is `stacks/saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md`. Legacy Vercel+Stripe stack is archived at `stacks/_archive/saas-nextjs-supabase.md` — do not auto-load.
223	- **Rule:** For any Boldteq internal SaaS build, the stack is non-negotiable: Next.js 16.2.3, React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, Supabase (SSR), Dodo Payments (never Stripe for internal), Railway (never Vercel), BullMQ + Redis for jobs. Stack B (Shopify) uses Shopify Billing API — never Dodo, never Stripe.
224	- **Applies to:** Arya, Riko, Koda, Rex, Bolt.
225	
226	---
227	
228	## How to Add Entries
229	
230	When Yash corrects any agent behavior:
231	1. Mira logs it here with date, context, rule, and affected agents
232	2. Mira updates the affected agent's memory references if needed
233	3. Pattern gets added to relevant `patterns/good/` or `patterns/avoid/` file
234	4. Next session, all agents pick up the correction via memory load
235	
236	---
